generationMethod: manual repository inspection + isolated local SSR observation
evidenceNotes: No risk is CLOSED. A risk may only be closed with evidence that the specific failure was measured absent; none of these failures has been measured absent in a live environment.
Several current-state observations come from an isolated local SSR run on 2026-11-02 with a disposable database; they describe the frozen base, not production.
Search Console is unavailable, so indexation outcomes cannot be measured: the register states that limitation instead of inventing coverage numbers.

items.description: An already indexed Spanish URL is changed, merged, retired or renamed without a decision, so the address that carries the existing organic traffic stops serving the same entity.
items.mitigation: D03 and D07 fix KEEP_AS_IS for every existing public URL and D15 Phase 0 freezes the URL snapshot before any change. Phase 4 compares the candidate against the snapshot and any difference that is not an authorised change blocks the phase.
items.rollbackTrigger: Any preserved URL returns a non-200 status, resolves to a different entity, or is absent from the released URL set.
items.detectionMethod: Snapshot vs candidate diff; status, canonical and entity identity check per URL family.

items.description: A second redirect hop is introduced (for example a legacy path pointing at a path that itself redirects), creating a chain that wastes crawl budget and can lose the original referrer.
items.mitigation: D07 keeps exactly three single-hop 301s and states that no new redirect may be added for an existing Spanish URL. The redirect map records one-hop destinations only, and the dataset is machine-checked against loops and chains.
items.rollbackTrigger: A redirect resolves through more than one hop, or a destination is itself a redirect source.
items.detectionMethod: Single-hop follow of every redirect source with hop counting; dataset graph walk.

items.description: A redirect loop is created between two paths (A to B and B to A), or a redirect points at itself, leaving crawlers and users in an unresolvable cycle.
items.mitigation: The redirect map is a closed graph of three sources with destinations that are never sources; Phase 4 re-walks the graph before release.
items.rollbackTrigger: Any cycle detected in the redirect graph, or a source equal to its destination.
items.detectionMethod: Graph walk over every 301/308 record with visited-set detection.

items.description: A redirect or canonical crosses locales incorrectly (Spanish URL redirected to an English URL or vice versa), so the language signal and the entity identity disagree.
items.mitigation: D07 requires sourceLocale to equal destinationLocale on every active record; D08 requires a self-referencing canonical per locale derived from LOCALIZED_ROUTES. The dataset and validator enforce both.
items.rollbackTrigger: A redirect whose source and destination locales differ, or a canonical pointing at the other locale.
items.detectionMethod: Per-record locale comparison; canonical equals the registry URL for that locale.

items.description: Premature MAREA exposure: a MAREA page, title, description, navigation entry, breadcrumb, JSON-LD brand or og:image becomes publicly reachable and indexable before trademark clearance and the public-use decision, converting an internal concept into a public brand claim.
items.mitigation: D-003 and D-059 set MAREA_PUBLIC_USE = NO_GO. The 23 proposed routes stay PROPOSED_INTERNAL_NOT_DEPLOYABLE, are 404 in the current build (observed), are BLOCKED_NO_CANONICAL and are excluded from every sitemap-eligible class. D15 Phase 2 is a hard prerequisite for any MAREA page.
items.rollbackTrigger: Any /marea or /en/marea URL answering 200, appearing in the sitemap, receiving an internal navigation link, or being named in public metadata or JSON-LD.
items.detectionMethod: Sitemap and route crawl for /marea prefixes; metadata scan for the MAREA token on live pages; link-graph check for live navigation edges to proposed routes.

items.description: A canonical, alternate or sitemap entry points at a blocked, unpublished or non-existent page, so the site advertises URLs that must not be indexed and dilutes the real page.
items.mitigation: D08 sets BLOCKED_NO_CANONICAL for every proposed page with no alternates and no group. The sitemap alternates are emitted only when both locale URLs are published. The unknown product slug drops canonical and alternates and answers 404 (observed).
items.rollbackTrigger: Any canonical or alternate whose target is 404, blocklisted by policy, or absent from the published URL set.
items.detectionMethod: Resolve every canonical and alternate target against the published URL set and the route registry.

items.description: A brand-publication bypass: MAREA reaches the public surface through an indirect channel such as a social preview image, a footer attribution, an Organization name, an og:locale block, a print asset URL or a document title, without any page being created.
items.mitigation: D-059 applies the stricter MC-14 rule over inherited allowances; D10 forbids MAREA in any JSON-LD brand or Organization field; D15 Phase 2 forbids MAREA in metadata, navigation and social previews. The claims policy and the brand validator are the enforcement points.
items.rollbackTrigger: The MAREA token appears in a public HTML document, a public JSON-LD node, a public image asset name or a public metadata field.
items.detectionMethod: Public metadata and asset scan for the MAREA token; structured-data dump review; social-preview inspection.

items.description: Structured-data claim inflation: a JSON-LD node states a price, availability, certification, rating, review or performance figure that the visible page, the gates or the evidence do not support, or states a MAREA Product/Offer that does not exist.
items.mitigation: D10 lists ten absolute restrictions and forbids MAREA Product/Offer, price, availability, seller invention, ratings, reviews, certifications and any claim stronger than visible copy. Product eligibility is gated independently of page publication. The inherited SEO gate whitelists the allowed @type set.
items.rollbackTrigger: Any JSON-LD node outside the whitelist, any MAREA Product/Offer, any price or availability value for MAREA, any aggregateRating/review, or any claim absent from the rendered copy.
items.detectionMethod: JSON-LD extraction from every published page; type whitelist; token scan for price/availability/rating/certification; manual claim-to-copy comparison for changed pages.

items.description: Hreflang reciprocity breaks: one locale declares an alternate that the other does not return, a group mixes entities, or a page declares a group without both locales, so search engines discard the cluster.
items.mitigation: D08 derives alternates from LOCALIZED_ROUTES through pageSeo() so reciprocity is structural, declares 15 reciprocal self-referencing groups, and forbids any group on an unpublished or untranslatable page. Phase 4 verifies reciprocity per cluster.
items.rollbackTrigger: Any alternate without a reciprocal return, any group with a single locale, or any group spanning two entities.
items.detectionMethod: Cluster walk over every page's alternate set; group membership and entity comparison.

items.description: An invented English alternate is declared for an entity that has no English content (for example an ES-only shop product), so the EN URL is advertised as the translation of a page that only exists in Spanish.
items.mitigation: D08 records ES-only products with zero alternates and an EN URL that is noindex; the observed behaviour on 2026-11-02 is that /tienda/<es-only> declares only the es alternate and /en/shop/<es-only> declares no alternates. The dataset forbids an EN alternate for shopDetail.
items.rollbackTrigger: An EN alternate on an ES-only entity, or an EN URL admitted to the sitemap without complete EN text.
items.detectionMethod: Compare each product's EN completeness with its alternate declarations and sitemap membership.

items.description: Sitemap pollution: a blocked MAREA route, a private page, an admin page, a sample page or a 404 target enters the sitemap, or the sitemap advertises a URL that is noindex.
items.mitigation: D09 defines 14 indexation classes with 4 eligible surfaces, all pre-existing; the sitemap generator walks prerendered output plus active products and never adds a private or blocked surface (observed: 98 URLs clean, 101 with fixtures, zero private/admin/sample//marea entries).
items.rollbackTrigger: A sitemap URL that is noindex, private, admin, sample, 404, or under /marea while that surface is blocked.
items.detectionMethod: Sitemap set diff against the expected URL set; per-URL robots check; prefix scan for blocked surfaces.

items.description: A soft-404: a missing entity answers 200 (an empty shell, a product-not-found page, a fallback template) so search engines index an empty page, or an unknown path silently returns the home page.
items.mitigation: D09 requires a real 404 with a noindex meta on the wildcard surface and forbids a home swallow. The observed behaviour on 2026-11-02 is 404 for /marea, /en/marea and /productos/does-not-exist with no Location header, and shopDetail drops canonical and alternates when the product is missing.
items.rollbackTrigger: A non-existent URL answering 200, an unknown path returning the home page, or a 404 page declaring a canonical.
items.detectionMethod: Status sampling over retired, blocked and unknown paths; canonical presence check on 404 responses.

items.description: Crawl-depth regression: pages move deeper, lose their internal links, or a navigation restructure orphans existing sections, so crawl frequency and discovery of the preserved URL set drops.
items.mitigation: D12 records the navigation and link graph; D08 keeps breadcrumb parents within four levels; D15 Phase 1 requires a collision and link plan per candidate. Phase 4 samples internal reachability for the preserved families.
items.rollbackTrigger: An existing section loses all incoming internal links, or a preserved URL becomes reachable only through a redirect or a sitemap entry.
items.detectionMethod: Internal link graph reconstruction from rendered pages; orphan detection per route id.

items.description: Invalid JSON-LD: malformed JSON, a duplicate @context, a script tag that breaks parsing, or a node type the whitelist does not allow, so search engines ignore or misread the markup.
items.mitigation: SeoService serialises with JSON.stringify and one @context per node; the inherited SEO gate parses every page's JSON-LD and fails on an unexpected @type or an unparsable block. Phase 4 reruns that parse over the full published surface.
items.rollbackTrigger: Any page whose JSON-LD cannot be parsed, or that emits a type outside the whitelist.
items.detectionMethod: JSON.parse of every ld+json block; @type whitelist comparison.

items.description: Query-string or fragment loss on a redirect: campaign parameters, filters or anchors are dropped, so attribution breaks and the redirect does not deliver the user to the intended state.
items.mitigation: Recorded as a measured current behaviour, not a hypothesis: /productos?x=1 and /open-marine?utm=1 both return location /tecnologia with no query string (2026-11-02). D07 records queryHandling as DROPPED_OBSERVED and D16 makes query preservation a mandatory check on any future authorised redirect. No fix is applied in MC-15 because it would change live behaviour.
items.rollbackTrigger: A redirect that emits no query string when the source had one, on a redirect whose specification requires preservation.
items.detectionMethod: Request every redirect source with a marker query parameter and inspect the Location header.

items.description: A redirect points at a private page, a login form or an account area as a substitute for missing content, so a crawler and a customer both land on a page that cannot serve the intent.
items.mitigation: D07 forbids any redirect to login, account or admin; the active record set has no such destination and Phase 4 re-checks the destination set. D09 keeps those surfaces noindex and out of the sitemap.
items.rollbackTrigger: Any redirect destination on a private or admin surface.
items.detectionMethod: Destination set comparison against the private and admin route ids.

items.description: Duplicate or near-duplicate content competes with itself: two URLs serving the same entity without a canonical, ES text duplicated under an EN URL, or a new MAREA page reusing existing technology copy.
affectedSurfaces: proposed MAREA pages reusing technology copy
items.mitigation: D08 requires a self canonical per locale and forbids an alternate to an untranslated page; D10 forbids reusing an existing entity identity for a MAREA page; D15 Phase 3 requires locale parity in the implementation. The EN URL of an ES-only product is noindex (observed).
items.rollbackTrigger: Two indexable URLs for the same entity without a canonical relationship, or an EN page serving untranslated Spanish copy while indexable.
items.detectionMethod: Canonical relationship audit per entity; EN page language check against content completeness.

items.description: Rollback is impossible because it depends on an invented deployment or release identifier, an unversioned redirect configuration, an unavailable previous sitemap or an application artefact that cannot be rebuilt.
items.mitigation: D16 defines rollback in terms of versioned, verifiable artefacts only: the git commit SHA of the branch, a build artefact checksum, the redirect-map dataset version, the captured sitemap, the Phase 0 URL snapshot and the database schema version. No deployment or release identifier is invented, and the rollback readiness is declared false until those artefacts exist.
items.rollbackTrigger: A release attempt whose rollback prerequisites are not all verifiable.
items.detectionMethod: Rollback prerequisite checklist completed before release, not during an incident.

items.description: A public navigation entry, footer link, breadcrumb or in-copy link exposes a blocked proposed route, creating a crawlable path to an unpublished page and signalling an unapproved brand surface.
items.mitigation: D12 must mark every edge to a proposed route as planned-not-live, and D15 Phase 1 forbids exposing a candidate in live navigation. Phase 4 samples live navigation for proposed-route hrefs while those routes are blocked.
items.rollbackTrigger: A live navigation, footer or breadcrumb link to a route id that is not published.
items.detectionMethod: Rendered-link extraction compared against the published route set.

items.description: robots.txt is used as an indexation control: a page that must not rank is Disallowed instead of noindexed, so it can still be indexed from external links and its noindex can never be read.
items.mitigation: D09 states explicitly that robots.txt blocking is not a substitute for noindex, records the current robots.txt (Allow /, Disallow /api/, sitemap line) and keeps private and admin surfaces crawlable but noindexed with the header. Any robots.txt change is a public change and is not authorised in MC-15.
items.rollbackTrigger: A Disallow rule covering an HTML page that must be de-indexed, or a Disallow rule added for an unpublished MAREA path.
items.detectionMethod: robots.txt review against the indexation classes; per-surface noindex verification.

items.description: ES and EN diverge in claim strength, metadata intent, structured-data content or canonical policy, so one locale promises something the other does not and a translation becomes a different, unapproved claim.
items.mitigation: D08 and D11 fix the per-locale metadata and canonical policy; the MC-14 claims policy treats semantic drift as a prohibited claim; D15 Phase 3 requires locale parity verification and Phase 4 samples both locales of every changed page.
items.rollbackTrigger: A changed page whose ES and EN versions differ in claim class, numbers, negation or structured-data content.
items.detectionMethod: Paired-locale review of rendered copy and JSON-LD for every changed page.

items.description: Indexation and post-release outcomes cannot be measured: no Search Console access exists, so success, regression and rollback completeness remain unprovable and any reported coverage number would be invented.
items.mitigation: Every indexation statement in MC-15 is INDEXATION_UNVERIFIED. D15 Phase 6 requires measurement access as an entry criterion and allows a declared reduced mode without it. D16 requires rollback verification against the local Phase 0 snapshot so that completeness never depends on Search Console.
items.rollbackTrigger: Not a failure trigger but a permanent caveat: no report may assert indexation, coverage or ranking without a named measurement source.
items.detectionMethod: Evidence-class audit of every indexation claim; presence check for a measurement export before accepting a monitoring report.
